title: Compact-open model of transported overlap restriction
statement: Let $X$ be quasi-separated [def-pc-scheme], $W\subseteq X$ compact open and $V\subseteq X$ affine open. Choose derived localizations with common Hom universe $w$ on $V$ and $W\cap V$ [def-pc-derived-category]. There exist a compact open $U\subseteq V$, a derived localization of $\mathcal O_U$-modules in Hom universe $w$, an equivalence $e:D(\mathcal O_U)\simeq D(\mathcal O_{W\cap V})$, and a natural isomorphism $J_U\mathbin{\ggg}e\cong S_V$, where $J_U$ is ordinary derived open restriction in $V$ and $S_V$ is canonical transported restriction to the ambient overlap [def-pc-derived-open-restriction-maps]. No assertion concerning perfect complexes or lifting of morphisms is made.

source.place: Overlap setup; explicit open-range comparison using Mathlib exact restriction APIs

proof.text:
Take U to be the inverse image of W under V.ι. The compact-open intersection
criterion in a quasi-separated space makes W intersect V compact, since affine V is
compact. The open embedding V.ι identifies U with this intersection, so U is compact.
The induced inclusion U.toScheme to (W intersect V).toScheme is a scheme isomorphism.
Its exact module-sheaf equivalence transports the supplied derived localization on the
ambient overlap to one on U, in the same Hom universe w. Derive that equivalence to
obtain e. At the module-sheaf level, Modules.overMapCompOverEquiv identifies transported
restriction from V with restriction along the inclusion of the ambient overlap into V.
Factor this inclusion through U and the preceding scheme isomorphism; the restriction
composition isomorphism and Modules.overFunctorEquiv identify it with ordinary open
restriction followed by the equivalence. Derive this natural isomorphism using
mapDerivedCategoryCompIso and mapDerivedCategoryNatIso. This proves the displayed
comparison on every object and morphism. If the overlap is empty, the same empty-open
isomorphism and exact equivalence apply.

proof_origin.place: Explicit categorical implementation of the overlap identification, using Modules.restrictFunctorComp, Modules.overMapCompOverEquiv and localization transport; not the Mayer-Vietoris lemma 08BV

mathlib_searches.query: Restriction to an open subscheme preserves locally perfect complexes and vanishing homology stalks; affine supported extension plus shift
A perfect complex restricts to a perfect complex on an open subscheme; the direct sum with its shift has the same closed support.

lean.statement: theorem exists_compact_overlap_restriction_model (X : Scheme.{u}) [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] (W V : X.Opens) (hW : IsCompact (W : Set X)) (hV : IsAffineOpen V) [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings V.toScheme.toRingedSpace))] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings (W ⊓ V).toScheme.toRingedSpace))] : ∃ U : V.toScheme.Opens, IsCompact (U : Set V.toScheme) ∧ ∃ hD : HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace)), letI := hD ∃ e : schemeDerivedCategory U.toScheme ≌ schemeDerivedCategory (W ⊓ V).toScheme, Nonempty ((schemeOpenRestriction V.toScheme U).mapDerivedCategory ⋙ e.functor ≅ (schemeOpenOverlapRestriction X (homOfLE inf_le_right : W ⊓ V ⟶ V)).mapDerivedCategory)
